newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-VAN GAAL TO QUIT AJAX, "SPREAD HIS WINGS".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VAN GAAL TO QUIT AJAX, "SPREAD HIS WINGS".

text.p: Ajax Amsterdam coach Louis Van Gaal, architect of the Dutch champions' greatest triumphs, announced on Thursday he will leave the club at the end of the season.

"I've achieved everything I can with Ajax. I now want to spread my wings," said Van Gaal, 45, who took over as coach from Leo Beenhakker in September 1991 and led the club to the UEFA Cup in his first season.

"My contract expires (at the end of the current season) so I have the chance to make that step," he told a news conference at Ajax's towering new Arena stadium -- another legacy to the successes he brought the club.
Amsterdam-born Van Gaal, who joined Ajax in 1988, said he was eyeing a job abroad, although he did not have a new club to go to.
"I have told Ajax (my decision to leave) early out of respect for the club," said Van Gaal, formerly assistant coach and in charge of the youth team.
"My ambitions lie abroad. I would like to go to a club comparable to Ajax."
Van Gaal led Ajax to the Dutch league title for the last three seasons. He won the European Cup in 1995, the UEFA Cup in 1992, the Dutch and European Super Cups and the World Club Cup.
Last season Ajax failed to retain their European crown, losing to Juventus on penalties in Rome.
In 52 "international" games under Van Gaal, Ajax lost only six times.
His availability on Europe's managerial merry-go-round will interest several top clubs despite Ajax's current position in the Dutch first division, an unaccustomed sixth.
Spanish giants Barcelona have been reported as saying they want Van Gaal as coach, with new recruit Bobby Robson moving up to technical director next season.
Ajax chairman Michael Van Praag said no successor had been lined up.
A journeyman footballer, Van Gaal played for Ajax, FC Antwerp in Belgium, Telstar Beverwijk, Sparta Rotterdam and AZ Alkmaar.
Tall, uncompromising and a larger-than-life personality, Van Gaal earned a reputation for discipline on and off the field.

He is also largely credited with developing and expanding the club's much-vaunted youth policy -- which over the years has spawned Johan Cruyff, Johan Neeskens, Marco van Basten, Frank Rijkaard, Dennis Bergkamp and Patrick Kluivert.
